subject_session: 84 sessions, 15 rats (Long-Evans); one session/rat/day, 1x1 m square arenas
stated_limitation: Caveats: the layer II sample is the smallest (45 units, and only 17 of them come from sessions with the second tracking LED that head direction requires), so the layer II percentages are the least well constrained; layers were taken from the file-level histology annotation rather than per tetrode; and although sessions were deduplicated to one per rat per day, a cell held across consecutive days could still enter the sample twice.

justification.dataset: 000582 (Sargolini/Moser conjunctive EC) is the canonical grid-cell dataset in the expected species, region, and open-field paradigm.
justification.handling: Real streamed NWB data loaded into Pynapple with correct dual-LED position/HD reconstruction, speed filtering, spike-count inclusion criteria, and per-rat-per-day deduplication.
justification.analysis: Standard Sargolini gridness on an unbiased Pearson autocorrelogram with a proper circular-shift shuffle null and MVL-based HD tuning, all appropriate for the data.
justification.correctness: Every reported number (grid count/percentage, threshold, spacing IQR, stability, spatial information, and all per-layer fractions) reproduces exactly from the committed CSVs and is internally consistent.
justification.figures: Figures clearly show the bimodal gridness distribution, genuinely representative hexagonal example cells, and layer breakdowns with explicit sample sizes and units.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence and the write-up names the specific weaknesses of this result (small layer-II HD sample, file-level histology, possible day-crossing double counting).
